expo.name: Cal&der
expo.//scheme: Universal links carry invite tokens straight into the app when it is installed (Architecture.md §7.1, §13.9). The scheme and every machine-readable name derive from the domain, calandder.com.

plugins.photosPermission: Cal&der uses your photos so you can put a cover picture on a calendar.

plugins.calendarPermission: Cal&der uses your calendar so you can copy plans onto your phone, and bring events you already have into a shared calendar.

expo.//plugins.expo-image-picker: Without this the Info.plist has no NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, so iOS shows no Photos row for the app in Settings and a real build crashes on the first request.
expo.//plugins.expo-notifications: Reminders are local notifications and work in Expo Go today. Remote push does NOT: it was removed from Expo Go in SDK 53, so news about other people reaches the lock screen only in a real build, and only once there is a server to send it. The plugin is here so the icon and Android channel are right when that build happens.
expo.//plugins.expo-calendar: Same reason: NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription must exist before iOS will show the permission sheet at all. Reminders are switched off deliberately; the app reads and writes events and asking for reminders too would be requesting access it never uses. The code imports expo-calendar/legacy, not the package default, because the newer API in SDK 57 throws in Expo Go.
expo.//name: Display name only. The ampersand is illegal in bundle ids, npm package names, URL schemes and domains. The domain is calandder.com (cal-and-der), so every machine-readable form derives from that: com.calandder.app, the calandder scheme. @calder/core keeps its short name.
expo.//orientation: Portrait by default; screens that want landscape call unlockAsync themselves. Locking from the root layout instead raced the screens' own effects.
expo.//icon: Drawn by tools/icon.py: the ampersand on a calendar page. Regenerate there, never edit the PNGs.
expo.//associatedDomains: Needs apple-app-site-association served at https://calandder.com/.well-known/ with this bundle id before universal links work; until then the calandder:// scheme still does.
